questions.problem: Find the function $f(x)$ and the value of $b,$ given that ${\int }_{2}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[{(2+\frac{5k}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{5}{n}].$
questions.worked_solution:
A definite integral can be defined as the limit of a left Riemann sum as follows:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx
$$

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx.$

Notice that we're given that the lower limit $a=2.$ 

Comparing the given summation with the general expression above, we see that $Δx=\frac{5}{n}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\frac{5}{n}=\frac{b-2}{n}\,⟹\,b=7.
$$

Consequently, ${x}_{k}=2+\frac{5k}{n}$ and $f({x}_{k})={x}_{k}^{2}.$

Hence,

$$
{\int }_{2}^{7}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[{(2+\frac{5k}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{5}{n}].
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is $f(x)={x}^{2}$ and $b=7.$

questions.problem: What is ${\int }_{e}^{3e}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
questions.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{e}^{3e}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ the lower bound is $a=e,$ and the upper bound is $b=3e.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{3e-e}{n}=\frac{2e}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{3e}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(e+i\cdot \frac{2e}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(e+\frac{2ie}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(e+\frac{2ie}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is ${\int }_{2}^{4}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
questions.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{2}^{4}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=(x+1)^{2},$ the lower bound is $a=2,$ and the upper bound is $b=4.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{4-2}{n}=\frac{2}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(2+i\cdot \frac{2}{n})\,\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(2+\frac{2i}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[{(2+\frac{2i}{n}+1)}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[{(3+\frac{2i}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is ${\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
questions.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)={e}^{x},$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the upper bound is $b=2.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{2-0}{n}=\frac{2}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(0+k\cdot \frac{2}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(\frac{2k}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[{e}^{2k/n}\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the function $f(x)$ and the value of $b,$ given that ${\int }_{2}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[4{(2+\frac{k}{n})}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{n}].$
questions.worked_solution:
A definite integral can be defined as the limit of a left Riemann sum as follows:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx
$$

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx.$

Notice that we're given that the lower limit $a=2.$ 

Comparing the given summation with the general expression above, we see that $Δx=\frac{1}{n}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\frac{1}{n}=\frac{b-2}{n}\,⟹\,b=3.
$$

Consequently,  ${x}_{k}=2+\frac{k}{n}$ and $f({x}_{k})=4{x}_{k}^{3}.$

Hence,

$$
{\int }_{2}^{3}4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[4{(2+\frac{k}{n})}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{n}].
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is $f(x)=4{x}^{3}$ and $b=3.$
